subject: Cloud Computing
title: AI and Cloud Data Infrastructure
description: A quick, practical guide to AI and Cloud Data Infrastructure.

hook.text: GPT-4 was trained on trillions of tokens. The storage and compute bill alone likely exceeded $100 million.

buildup.text: AI training demands massive data pipelines, GPU clusters, and high-speed storage — all cloud-native services.

discovery.text: Vector databases like Pinecone and Weaviate are emerging to store AI embeddings, a new kind of cloud data.

twist.text: AI needs are reshaping cloud data architecture. Traditional storage tiers weren't designed for trillion-token datasets.

climax.text: Cloud providers are racing to build AI-optimized infrastructure. The next decade of cloud is being shaped by AI demand.

punchline.text: AI is the hungriest cloud workload ever. Data infrastructure must evolve.

quiz.question: What new type of database has emerged to support AI workloads?
options: Vector databases that store AI embeddings for similarity search
Blockchain databases that verify AI model accuracy
Quantum databases that process AI queries instantly

details.summary: AI workloads demand specialized cloud data infrastructure including GPU-optimized storage, high-throughput data pipelines, and vector databases for embeddings. The surge in generative AI has driven massive investment in cloud infrastructure designed specifically for AI training and inference.
details.whyItMatters: AI is reshaping cloud architecture requirements. Storage systems must deliver throughput that keeps expensive GPUs fed, and new database types like vector stores are becoming essential.
takeaways: AI training requires high-throughput, low-latency storage systems
Vector databases store and query ML embeddings efficiently
GPUs are bottlenecked by storage that cannot feed them fast enough

faq.question: What is a vector database?
faq.answer: A vector database stores high-dimensional numerical representations of data called embeddings. It enables similarity search, finding the most similar items to a query vector. Pinecone, Weaviate, and pgvector power semantic search and retrieval-augmented generation.

faq.question: Why does AI need special storage infrastructure?
faq.answer: Training large models requires reading terabytes of data repeatedly at high throughput. Standard cloud storage creates bottlenecks that leave expensive GPUs idle. Parallel file systems like Lustre and high-throughput object storage configurations are needed to keep GPUs fully utilized.
